{{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|Kasuga-taisha|qid=Q714559|lt=Kasuga Shrine}}, the accompanying {{ill|Nakatomi Tokikaze|de|Nakatomi Tokikaze (German)|ja|中臣時風|zh|Nakatomi Tokikaze (Chinese)|qid=Q140446035}} and invalid|qid=Q135491614}} settled in this Tatsuchi area. They enshrined their ancestral deity, {{ill|Takehazuchi|de|Takehazuchi (German)|ja|天羽槌雄神|zh|Takehazuchi (Chinese)|lt=Takehazuchi}} (the god of weaving), from {{ill|Hitachi Province|en|Hitachi Province|qid=Q1055353|lt=Hitachi Province}}.{{sfn|Nara City History|p=493}}<ref name="genchi">On-site information board</ref>{{sfn|Imperial Household 68}} The {{ill|Shizuri clan|de|Shidori-Clan|ja|倭文部|zh|倭文氏|lt=Shizuri clan}} are said to be their descendants, residing in Tatsuchi-gō and weaving sacred garments.{{sfn|Nara City History|p=493}}<ref name="genchi">On-site information board</ref> Since ancient times, the shrine has been called either “Shizuri no Yashiro” or “Hizuri no Yashiro.”{{sfn|Nara City History|p=493}}<ref>''Yamato Meisho Zue''</ref>

==Enshrined Deities==
* {{ill|Takehazuchi|de|Takehazuchi (German)|ja|天羽槌雄神|zh|Takehazuchi (Chinese)|lt=Takehazuchi}}
* {{ill|Futsunushi|fr|Futsunushi|it|Futsunushi|ja|経津主神|mni|ꯐꯨꯠꯁꯨꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Futsunushi|ru|Фуцунуси|zh|經津主神|qid=Q1107286|lt=Futsunushi}}
* {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|qid=Q317997|lt=Homuda Wake no Mikoto}}

==Shrine Buildings==
===Main Hall===
A three-bay nagare-zukuri structure with a one-bay portico{{sfn|Nara Prefecture History: Architecture|p=912}}. It is said to be a relocated former main sanctuary of the Thirty-Eight Sub-Shrines of {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|Kasuga-taisha|qid=Q714559|lt=Kasuga Shrine}}.{{sfn|Nara Prefecture History: Architecture|p=912}}

===Subsidiary Shrines===
====Wakamiya Shrine====
Situated to the right of the main hall, enshrining {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|qid=Q313119|lt=Ōsazaki no Mikoto}}.{{sfn|Nara City History|p=493}}

====Hebizuka Shrine====
Located in the northeastern corner of the grounds, standing somewhat separately.{{sfn|Nara City History|p=493}} It enshrines {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}, and is also called “Yasaka Shrine.”{{sfn|Nara City History|p=493}} The small sanctuary measures about 2 shaku in width by 1 shaku 6 sun in depth, and on a slightly raised area there is a “snake mound.”{{sfn|Nara City History|p=493}}

==Festivals==
* March: Kinensai (Prayer Festival)<ref name="genchi" />
* October 10: Annual Festival{{sfn|Nara City History|p=493}}<ref name="genchi" />
* November: Niinamesai (Harvest Festival)<ref name="genchi" />
* First day of each month: Tsukinamisai (Monthly Festival)<ref name="genchi" />

===Hebi Matsuri (Snake Festival)===
The annual festival is known as the '''Snake Festival''' (Hebi Matsuri).{{sfn|Nara City History|p=493}} A giant snake about five meters long is fashioned from straw, paraded through the streets, and then placed in the shrine grounds.{{sfn|Nara City History|p=494}} Offerings in the shape of snakes are also made, created from taro stalks.{{sfn|Nara City History|p=494}} Children’s {{ill|Sumo|en|Sumo|qid=Q40561|lt=Sumo}} matches are performed, and a sumo {{ill|Ema (Shinto)|en|Ema (Shinto)|qid=Q687288|lt=Ema (Shinto)}} from {{ill|1890|en|1890|qid=Q7832|lt=1890}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} 23) is displayed in the offering hall.{{sfn|Nara City History|p=494}}

According to a 1915 ({{ill|Taishō era|en|Taishō era|qid=Q329174|lt=Taishō 4}}) shrine survey, the festival at the time was recorded as follows:{{sfn|Nara City History|p=494}}
<br>“During the annual festival, twelve figures are crafted and inserted into the sacred offerings. A large torch (or straw snake) is also made and carried into the shrine precincts. As soon as the offering is completed, the torch is set aflame and burnt entirely. According to legend, in ancient times there was a giant snake that frequently harmed people. The great priest Ri (Li) Gen Daishi pitied the people’s plight, defeated the snake, and made the land safe.”
